video_matrix.container: hvc1 Dolby Vision profile Main10 HLG BT.2020
video_matrix.note: app requested 60 fps; HAL fps range 30-60; container reports ~30 fps because Dolby Vision base layer is 30 (dual-layer temporal). The camera restart reclaim scene fired here.

encoder was configured 7680x4320 HEVC 74 Mbps and the file wrote (128 MB), but the video track is not decodable off-device: the muxer emitted length-prefixed NAL units (vendor.qti-ext-enc-nal-length-bs) that this platform's MPEG4Writer does not convert, and it is not in MediaStore. Container audio is silent-room. 8K recording is not usable as delivered.
recorder started at 3840x2160@120 HEVC, then the app process aborted in MPEG4Writer with a FORTIFY write overflow (SIGABRT). No media produced. 120 fps recording crashes the stock app on this build.

the ten-minute sustained run aborted the same way as 4K120 (MPEG4Writer FORTIFY SIGABRT) about 3 s in; no media. A sustained 4K60 thermal curve could not be captured because the recording does not survive on this build.
plain HEVC 1080p records and plays; 24 fps is the low-light auto frame rate on the dark scene, matching v15.

microphone.method: phone played a 3 s DTMF tone through its own speaker starting 5 s into a 15 s recording; audio measured in 5 s windows
microphone.finding: the microphone captures live audio and tracks the tone in both Dolby Vision and plain HEVC; the near-silent windows before/after confirm it is not a dead or looped track

cameraopt_runtime.finding: the ported reclaimMemoryForCamera and boostCameraByThreshold ran on real camera events: entering 4K video raised the miuicam_video_switch_event scene, which killed only cached background apps above the service-B adj floor and wrote the cgroup reclaim once, exactly as the port intends

cloud_color_filters.detail: the camera app's CloudConfig database carries the decrypted camera_app_filter_leica module (73 filters, 6 flagged isLeicaFilter=true: Leica Vibrant/Natural/Monochrome/Monochrome HC/Sepia/Blue), and the Video top bar shows the 'Leica Vibrant' look. These are LUT color filters delivered over Xiaomi's cloud filter service and they work on this device.
cloud_color_filters.filter_module_choice: FilterDataSource selects camera_app_filter_leica when supportCvType is true, else camera_app_filter_none_leica

m3_m9_leica_essential.state: initially reported edition-locked; subsequently enabled on this unit by two properties
m3_m9_leica_essential.first_finding: Forcing only ro.theme_customize=LCC made the app run as the Leica edition but a native anti-tamper check closed it after 3s ('APK version error' / security_check_fail path); it fails the same way offline.
m3_m9_leica_essential.correction: Deeper analysis of MiuiCamera bytecode showed the close is D.W.run() calling the libHawk native RitIeKoenwCSqcPf(), skipped when F6.d.X (camera.debug.safe.check.disable) is true. With ro.theme_customize=LCC and camera.debug.safe.check.disable=true, module 256 (Leica Essential) appears, the app stays open, and a capture runs the on-device 'OEM Legend' style-transfer pipeline. The device keeps its real model. See leica-essential-20260910.

device_state: restored: ro.theme_customize cleared by a reboot, camera app relaunched normally, stay_on_while_plugged_in returned to 0, phone asleep
not_verified: 8K and 120 fps as usable recordings (they crash or produce a non-decodable track on this build)
sustained 4K60 thermal curve (recording does not survive)
per-lens focus, stabilization and effect quality (dark scene only; needs a lit scene and a person)
